name: Ginsberg NDO
aliases: Phase 3 OnabotulinumtoxinA for Urinary Incontinence from Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity
question: Does intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA reduce urinary incontinence in neurogenic detrusor overactivity, and does 300 U add benefit over 200 U?

design.population: 416 adults with urinary incontinence from neurogenic detrusor overactivity (multiple sclerosis 227, spinal cord injury 189) and 14 or more incontinence episodes per week.
design.description: International, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial

verdictNote: Both doses beat placebo; 300 U gave no clinically relevant gain and catheterization for retention rose with dose.
takeaway: In patients with neurogenic detrusor overactivity from multiple sclerosis or spinal cord injury, intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U and 300 U cut weekly incontinence episodes at week 6 by 21 and 23 versus 9 with placebo; catheterization for retention rose with dose.

reports.label: Phase 3 trial, 52 weeks
reports.citation: Ginsberg D, Gousse A, Keppenne V, et al. "Phase 3 Efficacy and Tolerability Study of OnabotulinumtoxinA for Urinary Incontinence From Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity." *J Urol.* 2012;187(6):2131-2139. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2012.01.125
reports.followUp: Primary endpoint at week 6 within a 52-week trial

results.measure: Mean change from baseline in weekly urinary incontinence episodes at week 6; each dose versus placebo
results.note: P<0.001 for each dose versus placebo.

results.measure: Change in maximum cystometric capacity; each dose versus placebo
results.note: Significantly greater improvement than placebo with both doses.

results.measure: Change in maximum detrusor pressure during the first involuntary detrusor contraction; each dose versus placebo
results.note: Significantly greater improvement than placebo with both doses.

results.measure: Change in Incontinence Quality of Life total score; each dose versus placebo
results.note: Significantly greater improvement than placebo with both doses.

results.measure: Median time to patient request for re-treatment

harms.label: Clean intermittent catheterization started for urinary retention, patients not catheterizing at baseline
Most common adverse events
harms.note: Urinary tract infection and urinary retention.

delivery.label: Treatment
delivery.value: Intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U or 300 U, or placebo.

delivery.label: Entry criterion
delivery.value: 14 or more urinary incontinence episodes per week.

delivery.label: Dose comparison
delivery.value: No clinically relevant benefit in efficacy or duration of the 300 U dose over 200 U.

reports.label: Extension, up to four years
reports.citation: Kennelly M, Dmochowski R, Schulte-Baukloh H, et al. "Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA Therapy Are Sustained Over 4 Years of Treatment in Patients With Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity: Final Results of a Long-Term Extension Study." *Neurourol Urodyn.* 2017;36(2):368-375. doi:10.1002/nau.22934
reports.followUp: Up to 4 years and up to six treatments

results.measure: Change from study baseline in incontinence episodes per day at week 6 after each of six 200 U treatments

results.note: Consistently increased, nearly doubling after treatment.

results.measure: Incontinence Quality of Life total score
results.note: Improvements consistently greater than twice the minimally important difference.

harms.label: De novo clean intermittent catheterization, treatments 1 to 3
Most common adverse events
harms.note: Urinary tract infection and urinary retention; no new safety signals.

delivery.label: Extension design
delivery.value: Completers of either of two 52-week phase 3 trials (this trial and its replicate, Cruz 2011) entered a 3-year multicenter open-label extension of intradetrusor onabotulinumtoxinA 200 U or 300 U given as needed on request, at least 12 weeks after the previous treatment and above a prespecified incontinence-episode threshold.

reports.label: Four-year completers
reports.citation: Rovner E, Kohan A, Chartier-Kastler E, et al. "Long-Term Efficacy and Safety of OnabotulinumtoxinA in Patients With Neurogenic Detrusor Overactivity Who Completed 4 Years of Treatment." *J Urol.* 2016;196(3):801-808. doi:10.1016/j.juro.2016.04.046

results.measure: Decrease in urinary incontinence episodes per day at week 6, by treatment year
results.note: Decrease ranged from 3.5 to 3.8 episodes per day across 4 years from a baseline of 4.3 per day (3.4 to 3.9 across the 200 U-only and 300/200 U cohorts).

results.measure: Reduction in incontinence episodes of at least 50% and of 100%, by treatment year
results.note: At least 50%: 87.6% to 92.1%; 100%: 46.3% to 53.2% (86.6% to 94.1% and 43.6% to 57.4% across the 200 U-only and 300/200 U cohorts).
At least 9.0 months (range 3.0 to 49.2); 26.0% or more had an effect of 12 months or longer.

harms.label: Most common adverse event
harms.note: Urinary tract infection, with no increase in incidence over time.

delivery.label: Population
delivery.value: 227 patients who completed 4 years of treatment in a 3-year open-label extension of onabotulinumtoxinA 200 or 300 U given as needed, pooled from the completers of two 52-week phase 3 trials (this trial and its replicate, Cruz 2011).

relations.note: Same toxin and route tested in idiopathic OAB at 100 U; this trial used 200 U and 300 U in neurogenic detrusor overactivity.
